newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Spain, Portugal agree to combat crime, drugs.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Portugal agree to combat crime, drugs.

text.p: Spain and Portugal agreed on Wednesday on a range of measures to combat organised crime and drug trafficking, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said.

"We will crack down on crime, drugs and terrorism with measures that will guarantee security and respect for the rights and freedom of our citizens," Aznar said after two days of talks in the Azores with Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres.

The measures, expected to be in force by next March, include closer cooperation between the judicial systems of the two countries as well as allowing police to enter the other country in pursuit of criminals, officials said.
The two leaders also agreed to introduce an EU extradition treaty as soon as possible, officials said.
The two police forces are struggling to contain increasingly powerful and innovative drug gangs which run cocaine, heroin and cannabis into Spain and Portugal by land and sea.
